What is a capital city, and what is its main purpose?
Every country has a capital city. It is where the government of the country meets. The capital city is usually the largest and most important city in a country. Its main purpose is to be the centre of government — where the country's laws are made and where the leaders work.

🏗️ Capital cities that were built on purpose

Some countries build their capital cities specially. For example, in the nineteenth century, Sydney and Melbourne were planned and built as important cities.

Canberra, Australia — the story the exam likes. The people could not decide whether Sydney or Melbourne should be the capital city of Australia. So they built a new city, called Canberra, to be the capital. Canberra is inland, about halfway between Sydney and Melbourne. In 1927 it became Australia's capital.
This is why "the capital is always the biggest city" is wrong. Canberra, Brasília and Abuja are not the biggest cities in their countries — but they are where the government meets.
The traps: Brazil is Brasília (not Rio de Janeiro) · Bolivia is Sucre · Ecuador is Quito (not Guayaquil).

🧭 South America map questions

  • The equator passes through: Ecuador, Colombia and Brazil.
  • North of the equator: Venezuela, Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana (and the northern parts of Colombia, Ecuador and Brazil).
  • Rivers on the map: the Amazon and the Orinoco. The mountains running down the west side are the Andes.

🌎 North America — the main ones

The North America fill-in-the-blanks: North America is the third largest continent. It is bordered to the north by the Arctic Ocean, to the east by the Atlantic Ocean, to the west and south by the Pacific Ocean, and to the southeast by South America and the Caribbean Seas.

Great Britain is the largest island in Europe. It consists of three countries — England, Scotland and Wales. Those three plus Northern Ireland are known as the United Kingdom. England is the biggest country in Great Britain; its capital is London and the people are English.
Capital traps in Europe: Switzerland is Bern (not Zurich or Geneva) · Turkey is Ankara (not Istanbul).
